clue.text: Trick by sure-fire winners in performances

parts.note: to con is to trick or swindle someone
certs, short for certainties, are racing slang for horses sure to win

explanation.surface: A racing scam pulled off by backing favourites at shows.
explanation.walkthrough: CERT (short for certainty) is British racing slang for a horse that is bound to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerts are musical shows, so they are performances given before an audience.

clue.text: Best picnic?

definitions.meaning: to best someone is to beat or surpass them
an outside party, an ..., as a picnic is

explanation.definitionFit: To outdo is to surpass; whimsically split it is an outdoor party or event.

clue.text: Derby and Leicester may be parts of it

definitions.text: Derby and Leicester may be parts of it

parts.words: Derby and Leicester may be parts of it
parts.note: Derby and Leicester are English cheeses, not just towns, served together on a platter

explanation.definitionFit: A selection of cheeses on a serving platter may include Sage Derby and Red Leicester.

clue.text: Do wooers mess about in a tree?

indicators.note: to mess about with letters is to scramble them into a new order

explanation.surface: Romantic suitors fooling around up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosewood is a tropical hardwood tree valued for its dark timber.

clue.text: Made a concession — but also drew a line so to speak?

definitions.meaning: allowed something beyond the normal rules

definitions.text: but also drew a line so to speak?
definitions.meaning: in geometry a line is a point extended in length

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means bent the rules; literally pulling a dot out into a line.

clue.text: Writer offering translation in prose — no professional

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the other
no here means the professional part is taken away from prose

parts.note: taken from the clue as written before trimming
pro is the usual short form of professional
a crib is a literal translation used by students

explanation.surface: An amateur author provides a translation of a prose text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' reads as a writer's job but is a student's crib; 'no professional' leaves SE, and 'in' sets the crib between those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a person who writes, historically a copyist of manuscripts.

clue.text: Cover provided by the female harbouring rebel

indicators.note: harbouring means the female holds the rebel inside her

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381

explanation.surface: A woman gives cover to a fugitive rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: WAT is Wat Tyler, leader of England's 1381 Peasants' Revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap or swaddle, covering something in cloth.

clue.text: Revolutionary politician's endless nonsense

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the letters are read backwards
endless means dropping the last letter

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A radical politician spouts never-ending drivel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims TORY to TOR, which 'Revolutionary' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot is a British informal word for rubbish or foolish talk.

clue.text: Indian city strike leading to a lot of stories

parts.note: to bang is to hit or strike
lore is a body of traditional stories

explanation.surface: An industrial stoppage in India produces many tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore, now Bengaluru, is a major city in southern India.

clue.text: Speaks absolute sense initially

parts.note: utter as an adjective means complete or absolute

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of sense

explanation.surface: Someone talks complete sense from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say aloud, a verb synonym for speaking.

clue.text: Very hot kiln, circular on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside says the circular piece wraps round the kiln

parts.note: a ring is a circular shape
an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: A round kiln is extremely hot on its exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAST is a hop-drying kiln, often round, seen in Kent in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasting is an informal adjective for extremely hot weather or rooms.

clue.text: Leader creating a stink, backed by German thugs?

indicators.note: backed by places the German thugs behind the stink in the answer

parts.note: BO is body odour, a bad smell
the SS were the Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: A foul-smelling ringleader supported by Nazi heavies.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a person in charge, the head or chief of a group.

clue.text: The time is at hand? It must be gripping!

definitions.text: The time is at hand? It must be gripping!

parts.words: The time is at hand? It must be gripping!
parts.note: the time shown on the wrist is held there by a band that grips it

explanation.surface: An urgent warning that the moment has come and it will be thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: A band fastening a wristwatch to the arm holds the time at the hand.

clue.text: Ending period of office leading independent country

parts.note: a term is a fixed spell in office
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A leader's tenure at the head of a free state is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Termination is the act of bringing something to a close.

clue.text: Sailor expresses disapproval of hard cap

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
a crowd boos to show disapproval
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A seaman jeers at a tough hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarboosh is a felt cap like a fez, worn in the Middle East.

clue.text: Guns unsatisfactorily carried by vessel

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the vessel

parts.note: an artery is a blood vessel
ill as an adverb means badly or poorly

explanation.surface: Weapons poorly stowed aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery is large-calibre guns collectively.

clue.text: Heartless automaton's basic cause

indicators.note: heartless tells us to remove the central letter of the word

parts.note: a robot is an automaton

explanation.surface: A cold, unfeeling machine is behind it all.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of a problem is its underlying origin or source.

clue.text: Talker is exceptionally bright but quite small?

indicators.note: exceptionally hints at an unusual form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker is very clever though rather short.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resembling a star twinkles brightly yet looks tiny in the sky.

clue.text: See Greek walk in stages to Athens

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the run of words stages to Athens

explanation.surface: A tourist told to see a Greek promenade on the stages of a trip to Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link word inviting us to look.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa was a covered colonnade or portico in ancient Greece used for walking.

clue.text: Comprehensive description of three blind mice?

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cut off their tails

explanation.definitionFit: Detailed means full of particulars; read as de-tailed it means having lost one's tail.

clue.text: Devon town kids going round a region far from the south-west

indicators.note: going round says the kids enclose the region

parts.note: tots are small children

parts.words: a region far from the south-west
parts.note: NE, the north-east, is the opposite corner of England from the south-west

explanation.surface: Children travel from a distant part of England to a town in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Totnes is a market town in Devon, south-west England.

clue.text: Helicopter transporting silly old bumpkin

indicators.note: transporting means the helicopter carries the other letters inside it

parts.note: chopper is slang for a helicopter

indicators.note: silly says the letters of old are jumbled

explanation.surface: A helicopter carrying a foolish old country yokel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helicopter' looks like anagram fodder for the answer, but it is slang for the aircraft; 'silly' scrambles the old, and 'transporting' carries that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a clumsy, rustic person, an oaf from the countryside.

clue.text: Month when male falls off bridge

indicators.note: falls off means the male letter drops away from the month

parts.note: March is a month

explanation.surface: In a certain month a man tumbles off a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch is a curved span, the structure of many bridges.

clue.text: Yell when son's denied the best

indicators.note: denied means the son is refused a place and removed

parts.note: to scream is to yell
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy shouts when refused the top prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its finest part, the elite.

clue.text: Explosive left to wreak havoc on one European capital

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive
to sink something is to ruin or wreck it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bomb is left to cause destruction in a European city.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: Effect of winter darkness? It will get daughter down

indicators.note: in a down clue, down means the daughter goes below the first piece

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is often called it

explanation.surface: A gloomy winter will depress a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' meaning sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasonal affective disorder is low mood caused by short winter days.

clue.text: I offer to meet them informally in the same place

parts.note: a bid is an offer, as at auction
'em is a casual way of saying them

explanation.surface: Someone proposes meeting the others casually.
explanation.walkthrough: Ibidem, abbreviated ibid, is Latin used in footnotes to repeat a source.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin footnote term literally means at that very location in a cited work.

clue.text: Stars in misery ultimately, in hell

indicators.note: the second in puts the final letter inside the word for hell

parts.note: Hades is the underworld of Greek myth

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of misery

explanation.surface: Celebrities suffering wretchedness in an inferno.

clue.text: Time being against us?

parts.note: the idiom that time is a foe of ours, read as a definition of the opponent

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an opponent or adversary, as in the saying that time is one.
